styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate matches the references on the primary density facts: 17 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well, with 0% near-flat coverage. Those numbers come largely from the small screen and button details, though. The cabinet body and side panels are broad areas in only about 3-4 purple steps, with little grain or per-pixel texture. The measured outline is 100% near-neutral dark edge pixels, while the Beodeul stall, hedge and well sit at 0-33%. Together with the uniform dark rim around the whole cabinet, this reads as the 'sticker' outline rather than a dark tone of the neighbouring material. Shading is shallower than the references, so it fails the Beodeul bar.

styleAnswer.evidence: The arcade cabinet is the right kind of piece, and its tile density is on par with the references: 17 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well, with 0% near-flat coverage. The weakness is the shading structure. The cabinet body and side panels read as only about 3 lightness steps (a base purple, a darker side and a lighter top edge), where the stall and well ramps run to 5-6. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the cabinet has a uniform near-black outline around the whole silhouette. The stall (1% neutral), the hedge (0%) and the well (33%) use tinted outlines instead. The lamp also measures 100% neutral, but it is a thin metal pole, which makes it a weak comparison for a full furniture piece. Texture comes mostly from the screen and button dots. The body panels are smooth with no grain or per-material variation. Overall it has the sticker-like outline and a shallow body ramp, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
